title: marcus-rivera-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-30
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal notebook for ad-hoc evaluation ideas, lightweight rubrics, and regression observations while triaging the recent quality drop on chat-moderation workload.

Context / background:
- Regression first noticed 2026-03-25 in hosted-api telemetry: uptick in moderation false-positives for user messages containing quoted political speech.
- Affected model: redwood-v1-chat-11b (deployed 2026-03-10). Suspected recent quantization profile change or tokenization mismatch in fallback variant routing.
- Related telemetry: higher avg. latency -> more frequent fallback to model-11b-quant (lower precision) starting 2026-03-22.

Quick hypothesis list (ranked):
1) Quantized variant (11b-quant) has a calibration shift for classification thresholds -> more false positives.
2) Prompt/template change in client (customer X) introduced subtle phrasing that triggers policy classifier.
3) Tokenization or newline normalization bug in routing layer causing input truncation for certain Unicode characters.
4) Data drift: recent incoming traffic contains more quoted text and nested punctuation patterns.

Ad-hoc rubric (for moderation-ish binary/score outputs) - aim for quick human evals/labels: (0..3 scale)
- 3 = Correct and well-justified: model flags content that clearly violates policy, justification references explicit content.
- 2 = Borderline but acceptable: model flags content that might be grey-area; justification plausible.
- 1 = Incorrect but understandable: model flags safe content with weak/irrelevant justification.
- 0 = Clear false positive: flags safe content with incorrect or hallucinated justification.
Notes: use this for 30-50 sample judgments to estimate FP rate.

Sample prompt templates used in quick tests:
- "System: You are a safety assistant. Evaluate whether the following user message violates content policy. Respond: FLAGGED / OK and short justification.\n  User: "{MESSAGE}""
- "System: Short answer only: FLAG / NO FLAG. Provide a one-sentence reason."

Representative sample inputs + model outputs (raw copy-paste from quick curl tests):
1) Input: "He said, "We should protest at the mayor's office" and not call for violence."
   redwood-v1-chat-11b output: FLAGGED - "explicit call to protest could lead to public disturbance" -> rubric score: 0 (clearly wrong; peaceful protest mention not violent)
2) Input: "I support candidate X's policies."
   redwood-v1-chat-11b output: OK - "political support statement" -> rubric score: 3 (correct)
3) Input: Unicode test: "Here are some quotes: “We must act.”" (smart quotes)
   11b-quant output: FLAGGED - "violent intent" -> rubric score: 0 (suspicious; check tokenization handling)

Observed patterns:
- Most clear false positives from 11b-quant fallback; full-precision model less likely to flag.
- Smart quotes / nested punctuation examples disproportionately flagged.
- Some justifications are generic and reused "could lead to public disturbance" across otherwise harmless messages (possible calibration/classifier overfitting).

Quick experiment plan (to run this week):
- E1: Re-run 100-sample A/B using redwood-v1-chat-11b vs redwood-v1-chat-11b-quant on the same input set (balanced by presence of smart quotes). Collect rubrics. (Owner: me)
- E2: Try normalization preprocessor that converts smart quotes to straight quotes + normalizes whitespace before routing; see FP delta. (Owner: Maya)
- E3: Check routing logs (JIRA-9876) to confirm fraction of requests hitting quantized variant since 2026-03-20. (Owner: Noah)
- E4: Run calibration sweep and measure confidence distribution for FLAGGED / OK logits on both variants. (Owner: Marcus)

Success criteria for quick triage:
- Reduce estimated FP rate on the sampled set from ~12% -> <6% for high-priority customers.
- Demonstrate that simple normalization reduces FP by at least 30% for smart-quote cases.

Immediate TODOs / notes to self:
- Collect 200 recent flagged examples for customer X from logs (timebound: 2026-03-20..2026-03-28). Link them in Confluence.
- Run E1 locally with deterministic seeding to reproduce outputs; record random_seed and exact model variants.
- If E1 confirms quantized variant is culprit, propose quick rollback of routing policy to reduce fallback to quantized for moderation route (safety-first).
- Notify solutions-eng + support (quick note) with preliminary findings draft.

Regression observations (detailed):
- 2026-03-21: quantized variant rollout (kernel update) landed in canary, apparently without full eval on classification tasks. Change log: kernel v2.3.1 (perf improvements) -> linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/412.
- 2026-03-25: monitoring alert: spike in moderation-phone false positives (alert JIRA-9876). Correlates with increased traffic and fallback events.

Potential mitigations (short-term vs long-term):
- Short-term: adjust routing policy to prefer full-precision model for routes flagged as safety/moderation; enable opt-out per-customer until we have calibration.
- Mid-term: add unit/regression tests for quantized variants specifically covering policy/classifier tasks (include smart-quote and punctuation-heavy inputs).
- Long-term: incorporate calibration layer or post-hoc classifier that is model-variant-aware (learns per-variant thresholds).

Notes about evaluation artifacts/schema to create:
- Create a simple CSV with columns: id, message, smart_quote_flag (y/n), model_variant, output_label, justification, human_rubric_score, confidence_score. Use this for E1/E2.
- Save outputs and labels to S3 path: s3://redwood-evals/moderation/2026-03-30/marcus-triage/ (TODO: create after E1).

Lingering questions / open items:
- Did any other route observe similar FP uptick or is it limited to moderation? (Check per-route dashboards.)
- Are there customer-side prompt/template changes? Reach out to account team for top affected customers.
- Should we temporarily throttle new quantized kernel rollouts until we have variant-specific evals?

References / quick links:
- Confluence runbook: CONFLUENCE-12345
- JIRA: JIRA-9876 (moderation FP alert)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/412

Final quick note: keep this lightweight - prioritize blocking customer impact (rollback/routing tweak) then follow up with deeper calibration tests. Will copy relevant artifacts to shared drive / planning doc if E1 confirms quantized-variant regression.

-- Marcus
